![A diagram showing a curve C1 and a piecewise linear path C2 connecting points P0, P1, P2, and P3.](770fa0497770252dc22b4fa902ebb384_img.jpg)

The figure illustrates a curve  $C_1$  and a piecewise linear path  $C_2$  connecting four points  $P_0, P_1, P_2,$  and  $P_3$ . The points are marked with black dots. The curve  $C_1$  is a smooth, thick black line that starts at  $P_0$ , rises to a peak, descends to a trough, and then rises again. The piecewise linear path  $C_2$  is a thin black line that connects the points in a zigzag pattern: from  $P_0$  to  $P_1$ , then from  $P_1$  to  $P_2$ , and finally from  $P_2$  to  $P_3$ . The labels  $P_0, P_1, P_2,$  and  $P_3$  are placed near their respective points, and the labels  $C_1$  and  $C_2$  are placed near their respective paths.

| Point | Approximate X-coordinate | Approximate Y-coordinate |
|-------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| $P_0$ | 100                      | 650                      |
| $P_1$ | 370                      | 180                      |
| $P_2$ | 610                      | 730                      |
| $P_3$ | 900                      | 320                      |

A diagram showing a curve C1 and a piecewise linear path C2 connecting points P0, P1, P2, and P3.

![A diagram showing a curve C1 and its control points P0, P1, and P2. The curve starts at P0, peaks, and ends at P2, with P1 acting as a control point above the arc.](770fa0497770252dc22b4fa902ebb384_img.jpg)

The figure illustrates a curve  $C_1$  defined by three points:  $P_0$ ,  $P_1$ , and  $P_2$ . The curve is a smooth arc connecting  $P_0$  and  $P_2$ , with  $P_1$  positioned above the arc. The curve  $C_1$  is the lower, curved path, while the upper path is a straight line segment connecting  $P_0$  and  $P_2$  through  $P_1$ .

| Point | Relative Position             |
|-------|-------------------------------|
| $P_0$ | Bottom-left endpoint          |
| $P_1$ | Control point above the curve |
| $P_2$ | Bottom-right endpoint         |

A diagram showing a curve C1 and its control points P0, P1, and P2. The curve starts at P0, peaks, and ends at P2, with P1 acting as a control point above the arc.
